section_summary: This section records a dispute over how the occupation authorities should revive Japan’s silk industry and sell its output. A memorandum criticizes silk adviser Peter F. Magagna’s approach, while Magagna’s letters, report, and supporting exhibits argue for greater raw silk exports, different testing and sales arrangements, and less reliance on the United States Commercial Company. The final page begins a separate memorandum opposing a large silk fabric export program because of tariff barriers.

subfiles.title: Memorandum on Magagna’s criticisms of the silk program
subfiles.about: An unnamed writer evaluates Magagna’s objections to SCAP silk policy and the United States Commercial Company.
subfiles.summary: The writer favors exporting as much Japanese silk as possible, including fabrics where markets exist, and obtaining broader guidance on future demand. The memorandum argues that Magagna has been uncooperative and that SCAP’s silk officials deserve support while Washington agencies develop better policy.

subfiles.title: Flood mailing cover addressed to John Carter Vincent
subfiles.about: A congressional mailing cover addresses material to the State Department’s Far Eastern Affairs director.
subfiles.summary: Mailing cover addressed to John Carter Vincent.

subfiles.title: Flood letter requesting review of Japanese silk trade arrangements
subfiles.about: Flood forwards Magagna’s correspondence and urges a conference on the United States Commercial Company’s role in Japanese silk sales.
subfiles.summary: Flood asks State and War Department officials, the United States Commercial Company, and silk industry representatives to review testing, shipping, and sales methods. He supports serious consideration of Magagna’s proposals despite personal conflicts in the occupation administration.

subfiles.title: Copy of Flood cable to Magagna conveying Gerli’s message
subfiles.from: Daniel J. Flood, conveying Paolino Gerli’s message
subfiles.about: Gerli warns that declining prices and sealed bid sales threaten the silk market.
subfiles.summary: Gerli urges immediate revision of sales procedures and suggests supervised direct contact with Japanese reelers.

subfiles.title: Magagna letter on occupation policy and Japanese silk exports
subfiles.about: Magagna criticizes occupation economic management and urges changes to silk export and sales policy.
subfiles.summary: Magagna describes food shortages, weak industrial activity, disputed export accounts, and what he sees as the United States Commercial Company’s obstruction of raw silk sales. He advocates larger shipments, broader testing and markets, civilian business leadership, and alternative selling organizations. He also challenges the export of Japanese cocoons to China.

subfiles.title: Undated Magagna letter urging replacement of the United States Commercial Company
subfiles.about: Magagna asks Flood to press for new silk marketing arrangements and greater authority over SCAP’s economic work.
subfiles.summary: Magagna argues that company controls are holding back exports, asks for market testing of 42 denier silk, and proposes civilian selling groups. He also seeks a larger business role for himself within SCAP.

subfiles.title: Report and Recommendations on Rehabilitation of Japanese Raw Silk Industry
subfiles.to: Supreme Commander for the Allied Powers
subfiles.about: Magagna proposes a coordinated program to rebuild Japanese raw silk production and exports.
subfiles.summary: The report presents raw silk as a principal source of foreign exchange for Japan and warns that nylon has reduced the long term American hosiery market. It calls for planned output, stable prices, regular shipments, broader export grades, centralized testing at Yokohama, and limits on domestic silk use. Magagna also recommends guidance for producers, agreements with other consuming nations, equitable payments to growers, and consolidated silk administration in both the Japanese government and SCAP.

subfiles.title: Washington policy cable on Japanese silk production, Exhibit 1
subfiles.about: Washington sets provisional policy on mulberry acreage and Japanese silk production.
subfiles.summary: The cable leaves acreage decisions to SCAP pending firmer food and silk export targets.

subfiles.title: SCAP request for silk advisers, Exhibit 2
subfiles.to: War Department, for the Joint Chiefs of Staff
subfiles.about: SCAP requests Paolino Gerli and Mr. Douty as advisers on rebuilding Japan’s silk industry.
subfiles.summary: SCAP asks the two men to advise on standards, prices, stabilization, and silk types.

subfiles.title: Bowles letter on decontrol of raw silk, Exhibit 3
subfiles.about: Bowles informs Flood that he has signed an order ending raw silk price controls.
subfiles.summary: Bowles reports signing the raw silk decontrol order.

subfiles.title: Flood reply to Bowles, Exhibit 4
subfiles.about: Flood thanks Bowles for exempting silk from price controls.
subfiles.summary: Flood commends the Office of Price Administration’s silk price exemption.

subfiles.title: Flood telegram reaffirming silk sales proposals, Exhibit 5
subfiles.about: Flood tells Magagna that War, State, and company officials reaffirmed their proposals and denied plans to auction silk.
subfiles.summary: Flood reports support for the original proposals and promises to back Magagna.

subfiles.title: Exaggerated Early Demand for Silks Seen, Exhibit 6
subfiles.about: The clipping discusses possible speculative demand and high prices after silk price controls were lifted.
subfiles.summary: Mills expect strong demand for scarce silk fabrics and possible price increases.

subfiles.title: Sources of silk industry statistics
subfiles.about: A list identifies statistical sources used for the silk analysis.
subfiles.summary: Lists government, exchange, trade association, Japanese trade, and published statistical sources.

subfiles.title: Reasons for a single raw silk testing house in Yokohama
subfiles.about: J. Kom recommends consolidating Japan’s official raw silk testing at Yokohama.
subfiles.summary: The memorandum argues that one Yokohama testing house would provide uniform tests, easier supervision, lower costs, and convenient access to shipping. It cites earlier experience at Kobe and international acceptance of Japanese official tests.

subfiles.title: Export Program for Silk Fabrics and Rayon Fabrics
subfiles.to: Chief, Economic and Scientific Section, GHQ, SCAP
subfiles.about: The silk adviser argues that tariffs undermine the proposed export program for Japanese silk fabrics.
subfiles.summary: The memorandum urges curtailing silk fabric production and exporting raw silk to the United States.
